content.text: I reviewed every input file, all ten draft sections, the numeral ledger, and all seven figure briefs, and built a limitation-by-limitation source ledger against the disclosure (the conversation file is a truncated duplicate of the disclosure and adds nothing).

input.summary: Full ledger built and traced. All 22 claims (1–12 apparatus, 13–17 second apparatus, 18–22 method) were traced limitation by limitation to affirmative disclosure passages: rail/flat lower face/upper face/longitudinal slot through the rail; printed distance marks beside the slot; fence at the first end, perpendicular, downwardly projecting portion bearing on the edge; releasable two-screw/two-hole mounting and reversal moving the projecting portion to the opposite longitudinal side so the same marked upper face is used from an upper or lower edge; removable spacer plate with parallel faces changing setback by its thickness without changing separation; two separate carriages with anti-rotation keys in the slot; one cylindrical bushing per carriage with a bore fully through the carriage registering with the slot; parallel bores perpendicular to the flat lower face; threaded clamp knob, shank through carriage and slot into a clamping shoe below the rail, clamping the rail between carriage and shoe, loosening to slide; per-carriage pointers aligned with their bore axes and read against the same marks, their difference being center-to-center spacing; transverse center index at the midpoint; shallow V-shaped sight notch in the second end aligned with the index and with a pencil centerline; hardened-metal replaceable bushings; rigid polymer or metal for rail, fence, carriage bodies, shoes, pointers and knobs; no motor, battery, sensor or network; and the full use sequence ending in lift-off with nothing left attached. Every one of the 27 numerals (10, 12, 14, 16, 18, 24, 26, 30, 32, 34, 36, 40, 50, 52, 54, 58, 60, 62, 70, 72, 74, 78, 80, 82, 90, 92, 94) means exactly one part throughout the description, claims, abstract and figure briefs; each appears in at least one brief; no brief cites a numeral absent from the ledger. Section-line designations are consistent: FIG. 2 carries repeated designations 3 at both endpoints of line 3-3 and 5 at both endpoints of line 5-5, matching the Brief Description, the FIG. 3 and FIG. 5 brief headers, and the detailed description's statements that 3-3 passes through the second guide carriage 70 and 5-5 through the first guide carriage 50. Schematic conventions (plain blocks for carriages, a plain round body for the knob, a plain rectangular fence body, generic graduation lines) are confined to the figure briefs, cover only parts the inventor affirmatively disclosed, and no application text adds an "any shape"/"by way of example" broadening to justify a rendering choice. Functional-surface geometry was checked specifically: the sight notch is described only as the source describes it (shallow, V-shaped, formed in the second end, aligned with the center index), and no brief adds notch depth ratios, which end is deeper, taper, angle, runout direction, contact topology, dimensions, proportions, or graduation counts. Background prior-art characterizations were not traced to the inventor, as instructed. Terminology required by the brief (rail, fixed fence, guide carriage, drill bushing, clamp knob, clamping shoe, spacer plate, pointer, center index, sight notch) is preserved and used consistently; the "fixed fence" lexicography in the description reconciles with the reversible mounting in claims 13 and 16; no means-plus-function language, no priority or government-support claim, no drafting notes, placeholders, open questions, or unresolved alternatives remain. One verified defect was found: the FIG. 7 brief gives two conflicting placement instructions for the fragmentary rail band relative to the workpiece and the drawing-area borders. No unsupported technical assertion was found in the claims, description, abstract, or the remaining briefs.

findings.title: FIG. 7 brief gives conflicting placement for the fragmentary rail band and the workpiece
findings.where: figures/FIG-7.md, paragraphs 1-2 (workpiece placement and rail band extent)
findings.detail: Within the same brief the workpiece 90 is required to be clear of the drawing-area borders while the rail band, which is said to lie on that workpiece, is required to run to the left side of the drawing area. Both cannot be satisfied: a band that reaches the left border must extend past a panel that stops short of the border, so the renderer would have to either run the rail off the workpiece or push the workpiece to the sheet border. This is a placement conflict only; the parts depicted (rail 10, slot 16, transverse center index 24, sight notch 26, workpiece 90, centerline 94) are all source-supported, so no technical content changes.
findings.evidence: Brief states: "The workpiece 90 is a flat panel seen from above and occupies most of the drawing area, well clear of the drawing area borders." and then: "A fragmentary portion of the rail 10 lies on the workpiece 90 and extends as a straight band from the left side of the drawing area to the right, ending at the second end of the rail 10." The same paragraph also states "The workpiece 90 remains visible along both long sides of the band," which presumes the band lies wholly on the panel.
findings.fix: In figures/FIG-7.md, replace the sentence "A fragmentary portion of the rail 10 lies on the workpiece 90 and extends as a straight band from the left side of the drawing area to the right, ending at the second end of the rail 10." with: "A fragmentary portion of the rail 10 lies on the workpiece 90 and extends as a straight band across the workpiece 90 from left to right, beginning at a ragged break line spaced inward from the left side of the workpiece 90 and ending at the second end of the rail 10, the band and the workpiece 90 both remaining well clear of the drawing area borders." Leave the following sentences unchanged.
